install-harness.goal: After the person clicks Allow install on this exact approval, install without asking them to type. Poll inspect until installed; a failed job offers Retry.

check-installed.goal: Observe version-verified completion after installation. Installing or failure does not satisfy this check.

sign-in-harness.goal: After the person clicks Sign in, open the provider flow. Keep polling inspect until signed-in; never type commands or handle credentials for them.

check-signed-in.goal: Observe the completed provider sign-in. A waiting card does not satisfy this check.

test-connection.goal: After the person clicks Test it, start a real round trip. Poll inspect for the completed receipt.

check-round-trip.goal: A connection is tested only when its real tool-and-answer receipt passed and it remains signed in.

pitfalls.failure: Installation fails or Neyvia restarts mid-install.
pitfalls.recovery: Show the plain reason and Retry. Never claim installation succeeded before the version command passes.
Keep polling the provider status; do not infer success from opening its flow.

frontier: A provider login, account permission or API-key choice must still be completed by the person. A signed-in card is not a passed round trip. Long-chat compaction checks are available on broker-backed Claude, Codex and OpenCode; Kimi and gptme use their existing isolated read-only CLI bridge.
gptme upstream documents WSL or Docker for Windows CLI use; a successful native version check does not establish that all of its tools work on Windows.

The requested uv Kimi route uses kimi-cli 1.51.0, the last functional legacy release. Version 1.52 is a migration stub; updates to it are blocked. The current Node-based Kimi Code CLI is a separate migration and is not substituted silently.
guidance: Install asks once for permission to download the harness and missing Node/npm or uv/Python prerequisites. The app runs installers hidden and shows Installing with the latest log line, then Not signed in or Ready after a successful version command. Missing npm uses silent winget Node.js LTS, or the official checksum-verified portable Node distribution when App Installer is absent; missing uv uses winget or the backend Python bootstrap. Neither needs a terminal command from the person.

Sign in opens the provider-owned flow with one click. Authentication remains the provider's responsibility; the card detects completion automatically and offers Test it. Stop waiting only stops watching, not the provider flow.

Automatic harness updates use the existing hourly tool updater, owner Settings policy, NEYVIA_TOOL_AUTO_UPDATE and busy-process checks. Cards show when updates are paused. Managed npm updates retain the previous verified package; Python harnesses use isolated uv environments. Existing user uv and pipx installations are detected and upgraded in place only when present. Legacy uv Kimi is pinned to 1.51.0 and honestly labelled as no longer updated by its provider.

The desktop updater is separate. Its private GitHub release feed returns 404 without authenticated access. It needs an accessible signed update manifest and signed platform bundles, or an authenticated distribution service. Do not embed a GitHub credential in the app.
